## Regressions

None found in the design dimension. Checked: the kit move kept problemOf pure, and it was already called from the component in the round-1 tree (round-1 Screen.tsx:87); the zone that keeps a screen model away from src/shell predates the cleanup (round-1 eslint.config.js:127-129); every rule I probed fires on its planted defect and passes the allowed imports (P2: './strings' and './model.tools'; P3: the excused line); gate:lint is green on this tree (brief), so no screen imports another and no shell, screen or app file imports src/mocks, and per the brief every new canary went red once.

## New findings

verdict: NEEDS-WORK, one major and four nits. Worth keeping: IDS with run-time derived release markers, one useApi for every data hook, and the restated-literal rule are lean and reversible. ponytail net: about -13 lines and -1 file possible.

🟡 major  N1. The model-test exemption is wider than the owner approved, so 81 retyped copies sit outside the one reference file per screen
- key: eslint-rules/no-restated-literals.js#model-test-exemption-too-wide
- Where: eslint-rules/no-restated-literals.js:10 (`MODEL_TEST = /^model(?:\.[\w-]+)?\.test\.ts$/`, tested on the basename at :87) and :97 (any dictionary value is excused there); CONTRIBUTING.md:71-72; the decision analysis/metis-code-review/report.md:61 ("each screen has only one test, model.test.ts, that keeps hand-typed copy as the reference"); the plan widened it at plan/2026-10-10-frontend-code-cleanup.md:398 (model.test.ts and model.*.test.ts). Heaviest files: src/shell/model.sidebar.test.ts (30 literals), src/shell/model.header.test.ts (13), src/shell/model.problem.test.ts (11), src/screens/24-project-overview/model.states.test.ts (11).
- Why: Measured (a quoted literal equal to a distinctive value of a strings/en.ts or vi.ts, on lines that are not comments or test titles, in model test files): 127 verbatim values in 8 files; 46 in the one file the decision allows (screen 24's model.test.ts), 81 in 7 files it does not (6 shell model tests, 70; screen 24's model.states.test.ts, 11). probe P4: in src/shell/model.probe.test.ts, 'Registry' and 'Not built yet' pass and only the fixture id is reported. The stated reason, proving the model composes a sentence, cannot apply: a composed sentence never equals its template, so the exemption only ever excuses values the model passes through unchanged (1 of the 127 is even a raw {slot} template). Multiplier: plan C screens split model tests into model.<part>.test.ts files as screen 24 already does, and each new file is exempt.
- Fix: Narrow the exemption to the approval: test the path, not the basename, with `/^src\/screens\/[^/]+\/model\.test\.ts$/`; rewrite the 81 literals to read STRINGS (mechanical, the rule then lists every one); align CONTRIBUTING.md:71-72 with report.md:61. If the owner wants the shell pinned too, give it one model.test.ts under the same rule.
- approach-changing: no, one regex and a mechanical rewrite.
- trigger: the owner rewords 'Try again' (src/shell/strings/en.ts) at screen review; state: src/shell/model.problem.test.ts:20 and the other shell model tests type the old words and lint passes them; outcome: tests fail in files that do not own the copy and get fixed by retyping, the hunt round 1 named, and each plan C model.<part>.test.ts adds more of the same.
- guard-bypass: MODEL_TEST matches every model.<part>.test.ts in any folder and line 97 excuses every dictionary value in it, and CONTRIBUTING.md:71-72 states the wider version, so neither the gate nor a reviewer reading the convention sees a violation.

💭 nit  N2. The header's own contract cannot draw the header: the time zone lives only in the overview contract
- key: src/core/api/project.ts#header-needs-overview-time-zone
- Where: src/core/api/project.ts:5-21 (no time zone; the comment at :5 says another tab "can get the header without the overview response"); src/shell/model.ts:46-52 (HeaderContext.timeZone) and :252 (the saved time is formatted in it); src/core/api/overview.ts:40-41 (the only contract with timeZone); src/screens/24-project-overview/Screen.tsx:34.
- Why: projectHeaderOf cannot run without c.timeZone, so each plan C project contract must also remember a top-level timeZone beside `project`, or the tab reads the overview again; the comment at :5 claims more than the code gives. How Charter gets its header (embedded in each contract or its own endpoint) is still not recorded: spec 3.5 is unchanged and no task schedules it.
- Fix: one base in project.ts, `export const projectPageSchema = z.object({ timeZone: z.string().refine(isTimeZone), project: projectHeaderSchema })` (move isTimeZone there), and `overviewSchema = projectPageSchema.extend({ ... })`, so a project contract gets both by one extend; write "embedded in every project contract" into spec 3.5 with Task 16.
- approach-changing: no, a schema move with no change to the wire format.

💭 nit  N3. The screen kit's input carries the shell's own string back to the shell, and a screen model may not reach the kit's pure half
- key: src/shell/model.problem.ts#problem-copy-wiring
- Where: src/shell/model.problem.ts:20-25 (ProblemCopy takes `notBuilt` beside a Pick of the shell dictionary, commented as one of "the two strings only the screen can word"); its only caller, src/screens/24-project-overview/Screen.tsx:83-87, passes `notBuilt: shell.notBuilt`, the shell's own string; eslint.config.js:114-118 rejects a screen model's import of any src/shell file with "A model file is plain TypeScript and imports no UI, platform or mock layer" (probe P5: `import { problemOf } from '../../shell/model.problem'` in a screen model is reported by import/no-restricted-paths); CONTRIBUTING.md:191-193 lists the model ban without src/shell.
- Why: every screen will build the same copy object in its component and hand the shell its own string back (ponytail yagni: a parameter with one possible value); a developer who moves that mapping into the screen model, where CONTRIBUTING.md:184-186 puts such logic, is told that a pure shell file is a UI layer.
- Fix: add 'notBuilt' to the Pick at model.problem.ts:22 and drop the field, so a screen passes `{ shell, unavailableTitle }` (-2 lines now, -1 per screen); give the zone at eslint.config.js:114-118 its own message ("A screen model imports no src/shell file; the screen composes the shell's models") and add src/shell to the model ban in CONTRIBUTING.md:191-193.
- approach-changing: no.

💭 nit  N4. The string-literal collector is written twice (ponytail)
- key: eslint-rules/no-restated-literals.js#literal-collector-twice
- Where: eslint-rules/no-restated-literals.js:17-28 and scripts/check-web-release.mjs:17-27, the same TypeScript visitor (skip imports and type nodes, collect string and plain template literals); diff -u shows that only the argument shape differs; both are new in the cleanup (absent from the round-1 tree, grep).
- Why: two definitions of "the values a source file holds" for two guards that must agree on what a fixture value is; CONTRIBUTING.md:190 asks for a shared helper once two callers exist, and here they exist.
- Fix: export one literalsOf from a module both import (for example eslint-rules/literals.js, which the ES module script can import as CommonJS [Unverified - confirm before applying]); about -9 lines.
- approach-changing: no.

💭 nit  N5. design-system/fonts.web.ts is the one-value fork the new convention bans (ponytail)
- key: src/design-system/fonts.web.ts#one-value-fork-left
- Where: src/design-system/fonts.ts:1-10 and fonts.web.ts:1-4 (one value per key differs: the first family on iOS and Android, the whole stack on the web), with fonts.test.native.ts and fonts.test.web.ts; CONTRIBUTING.md:179 ("When one value differs, branch in place ... not a file pair").
- Why: the code contradicts the rule plan C reads, and the next one-value difference copies the pair.
- Fix: `const family = (stack: string) => (Platform.OS === 'web' ? stack : stack.slice(1, stack.indexOf('"', 1)))` in fonts.ts and delete fonts.web.ts (about -3 lines, -1 file); if the pair stays because the value is read at import, before a test's asWeb (src/viewport.test.helper.ts:10) can swap Platform.OS, write that exception into CONTRIBUTING.md:179.
- approach-changing: no.
